display.title: Episode 431: The King Is Watching (Summer Vacation)
display.summary_short: Before summer vacation: share Hashem and the Torah with new friends you meet; the Hakochainik march; Shema with a first-grade class; and the story of a rabbi who stops a coachman from stealing apples.
display.summary_long: With summer vacation a few weeks away, Uncle Yossi explains that travel, camp and visits abroad bring new friends, some of whom know nothing about Hashem or the Torah. That meeting is hashgachah pratis: Hashem chose you to share the most precious gift, the Torah. He shows children how to explain, step by step, that Hashem created everything from nothing, keeps the world alive every second, and gave the Torah as the way to a good life. Teaching another Jew is also tzedakah, for body and soul, and brings Moshiach sooner. After the Hakochainik march and tzedakah, children are reminded to choose a Torah-true summer camp. A first-grade class from a Crown Heights yeshiva leads the Shema with their rebbe. Story time, a lesson in honesty: old Rabbi Yitzchak travels through a forest learning from a little sefer, and his hungry coachman wants to take apples from the king's orchard and asks the rabbi to keep watch. As the coachman reaches the top of the fence, the rabbi calls 'He's watching!', and later explains that he meant the King of all kings. The show ends with Shabbos candle times.
display.lesson: Hashem, the King of all kings, is always watching, so be honest; and share the Torah with every new friend you meet.

date.note: Candles 8:11, Shabbos ends 9:21 fit Friday 15 June 1990; summer vacation 'a few weeks' away. One week after episode 430.

privacy.note: The visiting class's teacher is named in full on air; no children are named.

segments.summary: A rabbi agrees to keep watch while his coachman climbs into the king's orchard, then calls out that the King of all kings is watching.

quality.notes: The march, the class's Shema and some sound-effect passages in the story are not transcribed. ASR once writes 'Rabbi Akiva' for Rabbi Yitzchak. Camp line and candle times are period pieces. Fingerprint candidate: partial overlap with episode 393 (unchecked).
